items.prompt: Black to move, queen attacked. Name one of the three most common quiet retreats; the engine rates each within about 0.4 pawns of its best choice. Two of the common moves give check; think about whether a check helps.

claims.statement: Queen to a5, d6 or d8: all three are within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).
The check on e5 is worse than the best move by at least 0.15 pawns.
The check on e6 is worse than the best move by at least 0.15 pawns.

hints: Which squares keep the queen away from the knight's attack and from a quick harassing move?
Two of the common queen moves give check. Does a check from the queen help if the king can simply step aside or a piece can block?
Look at the a5 square, the d6 square and the home square d8.
items.explain: A check sounds forcing, but White answers it with a developing move, and then Black has moved the queen twice with the king still in the centre. The three quiet retreats keep the queen safe from the knight. At depth 16 the two checks are weaker by at least 0.15 pawns, a small price, but they give White a free developing move.

feedback_by_move.d5e5: The queen gives check, but White blocks with a developing move and the queen is chased again.
feedback_by_move.d5e6: The queen gives check on the open e-file, but White answers with a developing move and Black has still only moved the queen.

items.prompt: White to move. The black queen is on a5 and the white king on e1. Can the knight on c3 move at all?

claims.statement: The knight on c3 has no legal move.
One white piece, the pawn on b2, defends the knight on c3.

hints: Follow the diagonal from a5 down to the right. Which squares lie on it?
If the knight left that diagonal, would the queen give check to the king?
The squares are a5, b4, c3, d2, e1. Is d2 occupied?
items.explain: Between the queen on a5 and the king on e1 there is only the knight, because d2 is empty. If the knight moved, the king would stand in check from the queen, so every knight move is illegal. The pin costs no material, since the pawn on b2 defends the knight.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has played ...Qa5 and ...Nf6, and White has played d4. Is the knight on c3 pinned to the king by the queen?

claims.statement: The knight on c3 has no legal move.

hints: Look along the diagonal from the queen to the king.
Is any square between them occupied by something other than the knight?
Check d2.
items.explain: The queen on a5, the knight on c3 and the king on e1 stand on one diagonal, and d2 and b4 are empty. The knight cannot move.

items.prompt: White to move. Same position, but White's d-pawn is still on d2. Is the knight on c3 pinned to the king?

claims.statement: The knight on c3 has 6 legal moves.

hints: Look along the diagonal from the queen to the king.
Which square on it is not empty?
The pawn on d2 has not moved yet.
items.explain: The pawn on d2 still stands between the knight and the king, so the knight is not alone on the diagonal. The queen attacks it, but there is no pin.

items.prompt: White to move. Same as the first position, but Black has also played ...a6. Is the knight on c3 pinned to the king?

claims.statement: The knight on c3 has no legal move.

hints: Does the pawn move touch the diagonal from a5 to e1?
The pawn on a6 stands on neither the diagonal nor the squares behind it.
Check d2 and b4 again.
items.explain: ...a6 does not touch the diagonal from a5 to e1, so the pin stays. A move that changes nothing on the line changes nothing about the pin.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the white knight on b5 attacks.

claims.statement: The knight on b5 attacks exactly these six squares.

hints: A knight moves two squares one way and one the other.
Count the squares around b5 that are two files and one rank away, or one file and two ranks away.
The queen's square d6 and the pawn on a7 are both among them.
items.explain: From b5 the knight reaches a3, a7, c3, c7, d4 and d6. The queen on d6 and the pawns on a7 and c7 are Black's men under attack.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has gone back to d8 and nothing else of Black's is developed. Find a developing move.

claims.statement: Either 4.d4 or 4.Nf3 is within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice, and one of them is it (depth 16).

hints: Black has moved only the queen. What does that say about the centre?
Which White move takes the centre and also opens a bishop?
Look at the d-pawn.
items.explain: Black has made two queen moves and nothing else is out. White can take the centre with the d-pawn, which also opens the bishop on c1, or bring a second knight out. At depth 16 either is within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just played ...e6. How many squares can the bishop on c8 move to?

claims.statement: The bishop on c8 has exactly one legal move, to d7.

hints: The bishop moves along diagonals. Which two diagonals leave c8?
The pawn on e6 now stands on one of them.
The other diagonal goes through b7, where Black's own pawn stands.
items.explain: The pawn on b7 shuts the diagonal towards a6, and the new pawn on e6 shuts the other. Only d7 is left, so the bishop is nearly trapped behind its own pawns.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: ...Bf5, ...c6, ...Nc6 and ...g6 are within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).
...e6 here is worse than the best move by at least 0.25 pawns.

hints: Which black pieces are still at home?
Avoid a pawn move that shuts the c8 bishop in.
The bishop can come out to f5, or a pawn can prepare it with ...c6.
items.explain: ...e6 would leave the c8 bishop with one square, as the last board showed, and the engine rates it worse than the best moves by at least 0.25 pawns at depth 16. Several other moves are sound: ...Bf5, ...c6, ...Nc6 and ...g6 are all within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice.

feedback_by_move.e7e6: The bishop on c8 has one square left and cannot reach the good diagonals. The engine rates this worse than the best moves by at least 0.25 pawns.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the queen move that faces the half-open e-file and clears d1.

claims.statement: Qe2 is the engine's first choice at depth 16, and Bb3 is also within 0.4 pawns.
After Qe2 one white piece, the queen, attacks the pawn on e7.

hints: Which file has no white pawn on it?
Which queen move puts the queen on that file and out of the way of the rooks?
The square is on the second rank.
items.explain: On e2 the queen stands on the file where White has no pawn, so it faces the pawn on e7, and d1 is empty for a rook or for castling long. At depth 16 it is the engine's first choice.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: ...Nf6, ...c6, ...Bf5, ...g6 and ...e5 are within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).

hints: Which pieces of Black are still at home?
Prefer a move that adds a piece to the game or opens a line for one.
Several moves are close; pick one and test it.
items.explain: ...Nf6 develops a piece, ...c6 and ...g6 prepare a bishop, ...Bf5 develops it, and ...e5 challenges the centre at once. At depth 16 all five are within 0.4 pawns of the engine's first choice.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: Nine moves are within 0.3 pawns of the engine's first choice, among them Bd3, Bd2 and Bc4 (depth 16).

hints: Which of White's pieces are still at home?
Developing a minor piece is usually safe.
The bishops can come out to d3, c4 or d2.
items.explain: White is slightly ahead in development, and nearly every sensible developing move keeps the edge: Bd3, Bd2, Bc4, Bf4, Be2, Qe2 and some quiet pawn moves are all within 0.3 pawns of the engine's first choice at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. A file is half-open for a side when that side has no pawn on it. Which file is half-open for Black?

claims.statement: The e-file is half-open for White and the d-file is half-open for Black.

hints: Count Black's pawns file by file.
Black took on d5 and has no pawn left on one file.
The file is d.
items.explain: Black's d-pawn went to d5 and was exchanged, so Black has no pawn on the d-file: a rook there could press on White's pawn on d4. White has no pawn on the e-file, so a White rook or queen there faces the pawn on e7.
